en: Petavatthu, Uragavagga, 3. Pūtimukhapetavatthu The Story of the Foul-Mouthed Ghost Long ago, monks, in the city of Benares, there lived a certain man who was a merchant. He was wealthy, possessed of great riches, and had vast stores of gold, silver, and property. He was stingy, miserly, and avaricious; he did not give anything away, nor did he share with others. At that time, monks, the Blessed One was staying at Benares in the Deer Park at Isipatana. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, entered Benares for alms. When the Blessed One had walked for alms in Benares and returned from his round, after his meal, he set his lodging in order, took his bowl and robe, and set out on the road toward the southern bank of the river Ganges. Now at that time, monks, the river Ganges was full to the brim so that a crow could drink from it. As the Blessed One approached the river Ganges, he saw a certain ghost standing on the southern bank of the river Ganges. His head was like a human head, but his body was like that of a fish. His face was foul-smelling, and his mouth was dripping with pus. When the Blessed One saw him, he said to the venerable Ānanda: "Ānanda, do you see that ghost standing on the southern bank of the river Ganges, whose head is like a human head but whose body is like that of a fish, whose face is foul-smelling, and whose mouth is dripping with pus? "Yes, venerable sir. "Ānanda, that is the ghost of a man who, in the past, was a merchant in the city of Benares. He was wealthy, possessed of great riches, and had vast stores of gold, silver, and property. Yet he was stingy, miserly, and avaricious; he did not give anything away, nor did he share with others. Because of that karma, he has been reborn here as a ghost with such a form. Then the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, may the Blessed One show compassion to this ghost. The Blessed One then spoke these verses: "Alas! This ghost is suffering greatly, Tormented by hunger and thirst. He has no food and no drink, And he cannot find any shade. He wanders about in search of food, But he finds nothing at all. His mouth is always open and foul-smelling, Constantly dripping with pus. Then the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, what was the deed done by this ghost that he now suffers such a fate? "Ānanda, in the past, in the city of Benares, there was a merchant who was wealthy and possessed of great riches. But he was stingy, miserly, and avaricious; he did not give anything away, nor did he share with others. Because of that karma, he has been reborn here as a ghost with such a form. However, Ānanda, because he once offered a handful of rice to a monk who was practicing for the sake of enlightenment, he will eventually attain liberation from this state of existence. Thus the Blessed One spoke, and the venerable Ānanda, having heard the words of the Blessed One, was delighted and remembered them well. This is the story of the Foul-Mouthed Ghost. and you stand in the sky, suspended in the air;
yet in your mouth are worms and a putrid stench.”
"What deed did they do in the past that they eat [this]?
"I was a wicked ascetic of evil speech;
though appearing like one practicing austerities, I was unrestrained in my mouth."
Through my asceticism I have obtained the element of beauty,
yet my mouth has become putrid through slander.
This very thing, Nārada, has been seen by you yourself.
“Those who are compassionate and skilled would say:
‘Do not speak slander, nor speak falsehood;
you shall become a *yakkha* who indulges in his desires.’”
The Third Story of the Foul-Mouthed Petas.
